Display mock blog data in Main.tsx using this Blog component with the mock data: { title: 'Morning', detail: 'Morning My Friends' }. 4) Render Header.tsx And Main.tsx in App.tsx 4) The classname of title in Blog.tsx is 'blog-title', the width of blog-title is 'fit-content', fontSize is 24px

The project source root is `src/ui` (so `components/Header.tsx` means `src/ui/components/Header.tsx`); `src/ui/App.tsx` is the app's entry component.
portingNotes: Initial state = Web-Bench projects/react/src-init (App.tsx + App.css, unchanged; upstream index.tsx/index.html are replaced by each stack's entry). Hidden check = upstream test/task-1.spec.js byte-identical (saved as .spec.cjs only because the isolated verifier package is type:module); its `@web-bench/test-util` dependency is the upstream libraries/test-util (Apache-2.0) placed in the spec's node_modules, unchanged. Upstream runs it against `vite` dev server on src/; here against each stack's production server. Reference solution = Web-Bench's official final reference implementation projects/react/src (passes all 20 task specs upstream; vastly exceeds task-1), copied into src/ui/ref and mounted client-side from App.tsx; edits: React 19 port of utils/toast.tsx (ReactDOM.render/unmountComponentAtNode -> createRoot), a cloneElement cast in Tooltip.tsx, type-only imports - no behavior change. Only task-1 is ported because Web-Bench publishes no intermediate per-task states (task-N starts from the agent's own task-(N-1) output). Prompt = upstream description verbatim + one sentence mapping paths to src/ui. React 18.3 -> 19.3.
